# Matt Waldman's RSP Cast — 2024-02-22

**Raw transcript:** `raw/ingested/rsp-cast/2024-02-22-rsp-going-deep-with-brandon-angelo-and-matt-waldman-the-2024-rb-class-edit.md` (immutable — do not edit)

## Summary

*Going Deep* with **[[Brandon Angelo]]** (tracked co-host). A full running-back-class
episode structured in three parts: (1) what's genuinely hard to develop once a
prospect reaches the NFL vs. what's learnable on the job, (2) a round of
late-round/reserve-projection names, and (3) a round of names both hosts grade
as early-round talent regardless of actual draft capital, closing with a
"who am I not as excited about as everyone else" round.

**Framework segment.** Angelo's and Waldman's structured list of hardest-to-learn
running back traits — creating space as a runner, oscillating gears, reading
leverage in real time, and cultivated pad level — restates and sharpens the
[[Pace Control and Movement Intellect]] framework specifically for evaluating
draft prospects rather than veterans. The easier-to-learn counterpart list —
processing "the speed of the game," situational/down-and-distance management,
and pass-protection positioning (but explicitly *not* the mechanics of taking on
a bigger rusher without dropping your head) — is logged on
[[Prospect Pro-Readiness vs Ceiling]].

**Late-round/reserve names.** [[Cody Schrader]] (new) is Angelo's headline
pick — Missouri production plus Senior Bowl week. [[George Holani]] gets
Waldman's own late-round pick, developing along a Jeremy McNichols/Salvon Ahmed
line. [[Kendall Milton]] (new) and [[Kimani Vidal]] (new) round out Angelo's
group, with Waldman corroborating Vidal's movement skills specifically.
[[Will Shipley]] (new) is flagged by both hosts as underrated given his
receiving pedigree and speed, with the combine as the swing event for his
stock. [[Daijun Edwards]] gets independent Angelo corroboration of Waldman's
prior read. [[Rasheen Ali]] (new, ASR "Rasheena Lee") and [[Blake Watson]] round
out this tier, both praised for movement skill with ball security flagged as
the swing risk on Ali specifically.

**Early-round-talent-regardless-of-capital names.** [[Jonathan Brooks]] and
[[Blake Corum]] anchor both hosts' lists. [[Dylan Laube]] (ASR "Dylan Lobby")
gets Angelo's most aggressive grade of the episode — top five in the class,
built on a genuinely good outside-receiving profile — with Waldman ranking him
almost even with Corum. [[Jaylen Wright]] (new) gets a rawer-Travis-Etienne
comp from Angelo but a lower, ball-security-and-contact-balance-conditioned
grade from Waldman. [[Dillon Johnson]] (new, ASR "Dylan Johnson") is Waldman's
fourth name, praised for toughness and contact balance with an explosiveness
ceiling concern, and paired with [[Trey Benson]] (new) as the "need a little
nasty" archetype.

**Not-as-excited round.** [[Bucky Irving]] (new) gets a direct Devin Singletary
comp with real disagreement between the hosts on how close he already is to
translating it. [[Marshawn Lloyd]] (new) gets the episode's clearest bust-risk
case — ball security, decision-making, and a perception the hosts think is
inflated by a handful of highlight plays (see
[[Scouting Bias and Player Archetypes]]).

**Braelon Allen wrap.** [[Braelon Allen]] closes the episode: Angelo
independently reaches Daniel Harms's prior skepticism on competitiveness,
while Waldman frames him through a "Wisconsin curse" lens (Jonathan
Taylor, Melvin Gordon) and an explicit development-runway prescription — see
[[Player Development and Coachability]].

## Not given pages

Jase McClellan (ASR "Jace McClellan," Alabama RB — named only as one of
Angelo's three late-round picks alongside Schrader and Milton, no distinct
evaluative content given). Christopher Brooks (Miami RB, ex-Cal — a passing
cheaper-alternative comp in the [[Braelon Allen]] discussion, not evaluated
independently). Audric Estime (ASR "Audrick Estime," Notre Dame RB — a brief
positive competitiveness contrast point in the Allen discussion, not a
standalone evaluation). Devin Agin (ASR, unclear real identity — a single
passing mention paired with Christopher Brooks, no evaluative content). Kevin
Smith (former UCF/Lions RB — cited only as a historical "wonky mover" comp for
Bucky Irving). Spencer Ware (former NFL RB — Waldman's own self-deprecating
playing-style comp, not a prospect evaluation). Ronald Jones, Marlon Mack, and
Frank Gore (cited only as illustrative veterans in the framework segment — no
page updates beyond what's already logged on [[Pace Control and Movement
Intellect]]). Jonathan Taylor, Melvin Gordon, Chuba Hubbard, and Miles Sanders
(current NFL veterans cited only as comps in the [[Braelon Allen]] and
[[Marshawn Lloyd]] discussions — not tracked prospects for this ingest). Sony
Michel, Ameer Abdullah, David Wilson, and Stevan Ridley (historical ball-security
comps in the [[Scouting Bias and Player Archetypes]] discussion — not tracked).
Jauan Jennings and Kenneth Gainwell (comp names only, neither tracked). [[Rome
Odunze]] is mentioned only as context for how easy Dillon Johnson is to overlook
on the same tape — no new evaluative content on Odunze himself. Mike Leach
(deceased former Mississippi State coach — referenced only for the disputed
toughness-rumor video about Dillon Johnson).
